candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record features an elderly immunosenescent patient with bone destruction, cavernous sinus invasion, negative bacterial cultures, negative hyphae on histopathology (though fungal culture negativity does not exclude invasive fungal disease, especially in early or treated cases), and persistent inflammation despite surgery—all pointing toward invasive fungal rhinosinusitis as the final diagnostic object. C001 correctly captures the anatomical scope (sphenoid sinusitis with intracranial extension) but is a parent/descriptive category that lacks the required invasive fungal etiology specified in the benchmark reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Identifies sphenoid sinusitis with intracranial extension but omits the invasive fungal etiology that defines the benchmark diagnosis

case_quality_flags: Histopathology negative for hyphae and cultures sterile introduce diagnostic uncertainty for invasive fungal rhinosinusitis, but the overall clinico-radiological picture and infectious diseases referral support this as the working diagnosis
Culture and histopathology negativity may reflect sampling limitations or prior antifungal/steroid exposure rather than true absence of fungal infection
